evidence: Braun & Hogenberg, Civitates orbis terrarum I, 1572, “vulgo Lisbona”
terms.comment: The form the libellī use; Olisīpō is just as good. Cities and small places take no preposition: Lisbōnam volābimus, Lisbōnae sumus, Sintrā (from Sintra); countries take one: in Lūsitāniam, in Lūsitāniā.
The ancient name, which many Latin speakers use today.

lisbona.html: The long ō keeps the stress of Portuguese Lisboa on that syllable, by the convention for modern names (Olisīpō has a long ō in the same place).

sources: Georg Braun and Frans Hogenberg, Civitates orbis terrarum I (1572), as cited.
